column5: source
column6: target

column5: Now...! Go!
column6: 现在……！快走！

column5: In our haste, we still make sure to be as silent as possible.{w}\nThe Grand Library isn't too far away. In fact, I can see it now.{w}\nIt stands tall, and seems to be the one building that's not falling apart.
column6: 尽管行色匆忙，我们仍尽量不发出声响。{w}\n大图书馆离这儿不远了。事实上，我现在已经能看见它了。{w}\n它高高矗立，似乎是唯一一座没有坍塌的建筑。

column5: As soon as we arrive there, we all let out a big sigh of relief.{w}\nWe can still hear the fighting, but it's more distant than before.{w}\nThrough the screams, it's impossible to tell which side is winning.
column6: 一到那里，我们都长长地松了口气。{w}\n我们仍能听见战斗声，但比之前远了。{w}\n透过那些惨叫，根本听不出哪一方占着上风。

column5: What's going on back there...?
column6: 后面到底怎么回事……？

column5: I don't know. Let's just hope it's going well.
column6: 不知道。只能盼着一切顺利。

column5: Doesn't sound that way.
column6: 听起来可不像。

column5: For The Honor Guard, maybe.\nHurry up — we need to get inside.
column6: 也许是对荣誉卫队而言吧。\n快点——我们得进去。

column5: Shouldn't we wait for The Monarch Vessels?\nAt this rate, it might not be much longer.
column6: 我们不用等君主容器吗？\n照这情形，也许要不了多久了。

column5: Shouldn't we wait for The Seers?\nAt this rate, it might not be much longer.
column6: 我们不用等先知们吗？\n照这情形，也许要不了多久了。

column5: No, they can meet us inside.\nWe can't risk running into more suits.\nThat was just one group. I'm sure there's more.
column6: 不，他们可以进去和我们会合。\n我们不能冒险再撞上更多盔甲。\n那只是一队而已。肯定还有更多。

column5: Right.
column6: 好吧。

column5: They start to ascend the stairs, but Howl stops them.
column6: 他们开始登上台阶，但豪尔拦住了他们。

column5: Wait. The Library seems fine.\nWhy does it not decay like the rest?
column6: 等等。图书馆看起来完好无损。\n为什么它不像其他地方那样腐朽？

column5: Everybody turns to face him. But nobody knows.{w}\nDamek takes the stairs back down, and faces Howl.
column6: 所有人都转头看向他。但没人知道答案。{w}\n达梅克走回台阶下，面对着豪尔。

column5: I don't know — but I think this is a good sign.\nIt means we can control or limit what's happening.\nKnowing this, we might be able to fix Balteus.
column6: 我不知道——但我觉得这是个好兆头。\n这说明我们能够控制或限制正在发生的事。\n明白这一点，也许我们就能修复巴尔泰乌斯。

column5: Or perhaps it's a bad sign, Damek.\nMaybe our enemy has the power to harm Alestia itself.\nHow do you think we can stand up against such a foe?
column6: 又或者这是个坏兆头，达梅克。\n也许我们的敌人有能力伤害阿拉斯蒂亚本身。\n你觉得我们要怎么对抗这样的对手？

column5: Everybody exchanges worried glances.{w}\nBut then, their eyes find their way to the blade on my back.{w}\nIt's apparent that conventional means wouldn't be enough to win.
column6: 大家忧心忡忡地交换着眼神。{w}\n但随后，他们的目光都落到了我背上的那把剑上。{w}\n显然，常规手段不足以取胜。

column5: Nobody knows how to answer Howl, and an awkward silence follows.{w}\nBut then we realize that it is, indeed, a silence. This is concerning.{w}\nThe earlier fight is over — but did The Monarch Vessels prevail?
column6: 没人知道该如何回应豪尔，随之而来的是尴尬的沉默。{w}\n但接着我们意识到，那确实是一片沉寂。这令人不安。{w}\n先前的战斗结束了——可君主容器赢了吗？

column5: Nobody knows how to answer Howl, and an awkward silence follows.{w}\nBut then we realize that it is, indeed, a silence. This is concerning.{w}\nThe earlier fight is over — but did The Created Seers prevail?
column6: 没人知道该如何回应豪尔，随之而来的是尴尬的沉默。{w}\n但接着我们意识到，那确实是一片沉寂。这令人不安。{w}\n先前的战斗结束了——可被造先知们赢了吗？

column5: Hey, uh, let's get inside, alright?\nMaybe the Librarian knows more about this.\nWe shouldn't stand around in the open out here.
column6: 嘿，呃，我们进去吧，好吗？\n也许图书管理员知道得更多。\n我们不该这样站在外面空地上。

column5: Having successfully changed the subject, we start heading inside.{w}\nHowl made a good point, but none of us were able to counter it.{w}\nI doubt that the Librarian would want to talk to invaders like us.
column6: 成功转移了话题后，我们开始往里走。{w}\n豪尔说得有道理，但我们谁都没能反驳他。{w}\n我怀疑图书管理员不会愿意跟我们这样的入侵者说话。

column5: It makes me worry about how we might get them to talk.{w}\nThere was so much uncertainty and worry in the air right now.{w}\nAs we enter the Library, I hope that our forces lived through their fight.
column6: 这让我担心要怎样才能让他们开口。{w}\n此刻空气中弥漫着太多的不确定与忧虑。{w}\n走进图书馆时，我祈祷我们的部队能活过那场战斗。

column5: When we enter the Library, I'm taken aback by what I see.{w}\nDust fills the air, and it seems like this place has seen better days.{w}\nThe only sign that somebody has been here, is that the books remain clean.
column6: 走进图书馆时，眼前的景象让我吃了一惊。{w}\n空气里满是灰尘，这地方看来曾经辉煌过。{w}\n唯一能证明有人来过的迹象，就是那些书依旧一尘不染。

column5: Whoever has been taking care of this place only cares about the literature.{w}\nI guess that's acceptable, since that would be the main job of a Librarian.{w}\nBut it just seems odd. All the time in the world, and it's still quite dirty.
column6: 打理这里的人只在乎那些书籍。{w}\n我想这也能理解，毕竟那本该是图书管理员的主要职责。{w}\n但总觉得有些奇怪。有的是时间，这里却还是这么脏。

column5: There's some kind of weird apparatus in the back of the Library.{w}\nI've never seen anything like it before. It's almost awe-inspiring.{w}\nMy comrades all look around, sharing that same look of awe.
column6: 图书馆深处有个奇怪的装置。{w}\n我从没见过那样的东西。简直令人惊叹。{w}\n我的同伴们四下张望，都带着同样的敬畏神情。

column5: This is amazing...!
column6: 太惊人了……！

column5: I've never seen so many books in one place before.\nI wonder what they're all about. Should we take a look?
column6: 我从没见过一个地方有这么多书。\n不知道它们都讲些什么。我们要不要看看？

column5: Maybe not. We're here for a reason, remember?\nLet's find the owner, and see what they can tell us.
column6: 还是别了。我们来这儿是有目的的，还记得吗？\n先找到这里的主人，看看他能告诉我们什么。

column5: Howl steps forward, objecting before anyone else can speak.
column6: 豪尔上前一步，抢在其他人开口前提出异议。

column5: Actually, there's a chance that the books could tell us even more.\nThe Triumvirate must keep them away from the mainland for a reason.
column6: 其实，这些书说不定能告诉我们更多。\n三人执政团把它们隔绝于大陆之外，一定有原因。

column5: What do you mean...?
column6: 你是什么意思……？

column5: The Monarchy vanished in the blink of an eye. This, we know for sure.\nPeople can be erased — but not culture. Signs of our time here would've remained.
column6: 王朝在眨眼间就消失了。这一点我们确信无疑。\n人可以抹去——但文化不能。我们那个时代的痕迹本该留存下来。

column5: So you're saying—
column6: 所以你是说——

column5: Before he can continue, we hear a noise come from down the hall.{w}\nWe know The Honor Guard can't enter — so it must be the proprieter.{w}\nKnowing that we need to take them hostage, we assume hostile stances.
column6: 没等他说完，走廊那头传来一阵响动。{w}\n我们知道荣誉卫队进不来——所以那一定是这里的主人。{w}\n想到需要把他挟持为人质，我们摆出了敌对的架势。

column5: Looking into the past is one of the best ways to learn.\nIf we don't become better people, then we'll repeat the same mistakes.\nHow fitting then, that The Old Monarchy would focus only on the future.
column6: 审视过去是最好的学习方式之一。\n如果我们不成为更好的人，就会重蹈覆辙。\n所以旧王朝只盯着未来，还真是讽刺。

column5: We all exchange glances, slightly confused.
column6: 我们面面相觑，有些困惑。

column5: They wanted to guide themselves to the “perfect future”.\nIf it was possible to get there, then no cost would be too high.\nIn the name of a better world, they embraced corruption.
column6: 他们想引导自己走向“完美的未来”。\n如果能抵达那里，任何代价都不算高。\n以更美好世界的名义，他们拥抱了腐败。

column5: After a few steps forward, the mysterious man comes into view.
column6: 又走了几步，那个神秘的男人出现在视野中。

column5: Too often do we condemn others in our self-serving journeys.\nA bright future for The Monarchy would've meant death for other innocent worlds.\nThe Triumvirate chose to step in, as they have countless times before, to maintain balance.
column6: 在我们自私的旅途中，我们太常谴责他人。\n王朝光明的未来，意味着其他无辜世界的灭亡。\n三人执政团选择介入，正如他们此前无数次所做的那样，以维持平衡。

column5: Damek interjects, with a look on his face that I can only describe as the onset of anger.
column6: 达梅克插话，脸上的神情我只能形容为怒火初起。

column5: We know what The Triumvirate did to The Monarchy. Howl told us.\nBut like you said — mistakes are how we learn, and grow. It's how we become {i}better{/i}.\nIf the option of failure is taken away from us, we can no longer call ourselves people.
column6: 我们知道三人执政团对王朝做了什么。豪尔告诉过我们。\n但就像你说的——错误是我们学习和成长的方式。是我们变得{i}更好{/i}的方式。\n如果失败的可能性被夺走，我们就再也不能称自己为人了。

column5: They can hide behind whatever reason they want — but they're wrong to control us.\nThe ability to make these mistakes is our {i}right{/i}, and I will not stand by while it is taken away.\nCorruption? Death? Nobody wants these, but without them, we might as well not exist at all!
column6: 他们可以躲在任何理由背后——但他们控制我们是错的。\n犯下这些错误的能力是我们的{i}权利{/i}，我不会袖手旁观，任由它被夺走。\n腐败？死亡？没人想要这些，但没有它们，我们干脆就不该存在！

column5: Everybody nods and cheers Damek on.{w}\nThe mystery man shrugs, and keeps walking forward.
column6: 众人点头，为达梅克喝彩。{w}\n神秘男子耸耸肩，继续向前走。

column5: Restrain this man.
column6: 制住这个人。

column5: I expect to see the man put up a fight, but he doesn't.
column6: 我以为这人会反抗，但他没有。

column5: You will experience no resistance from me.\nBut on the other hand, you'll find no help, either.\nDo what you must, but keep the Library intact.
column6: 我不会给你们制造任何阻力。\n但另一方面，你们也得不到任何帮助。\n你们该做什么就做什么，但别弄坏了图书馆。

column5: He gets on his knees, and holds out his wrists.{w}\nHowl makes quick work of restraining him.
column6: 他跪了下来，伸出双手。{w}\n豪尔麻利地把他捆了起来。

column5: Who {i}are{/i} you...?\nYou know far more than most.
column6: 你到底是{i}谁{/i}……？\n你知道的远比大多数人多。

column5: The man shakes his head.
column6: 那人摇了摇头。

column5: Just a hoarder of knowledge.\nA man who preserves the past, rather than erasing it.\nIn exchange, The Triumvirate gives me life, and shelter.
column6: 不过是个囤积知识的人。\n一个保存过去、而非抹去过去的人。\n作为交换，三人执政团给了我生命和庇护。

column5: Another one of their victims, you mean.\nEternal life in exchange for servitude. Despicable.\nWhat atrocities did you commit in their name?
column6: 你是说，又一个他们的受害者。\n以奴役换取永生。可鄙。\n你曾以他们的名义犯下过什么暴行？

column5: I created this Library. A glimpse into the past.\nEverything The Monarchy ever wrote, is on these shelves.\nThat was my job. Preserve the old history, while creating a new one.
column6: 我创建了这座图书馆。一个窥视过去的窗口。\n王朝写过的一切，都在这书架之上。\n那就是我的职责。在创造新历史的同时，保存旧历史。

column5: And what new history did you create?
column6: 那你创造了什么新历史？

column5: I wrote about The Triumvirate, and spread it everywhere.\nI made them seem like Gods. Like they were the creators of this world.\nAs new life began on Alestia, they found my writing, and believed every word.
column6: 我写下关于三人执政团的文字，并四处传播。\n我让他们看起来像神。仿佛他们是这个世界的创造者。\n当新的生命在阿拉斯蒂亚诞生时，他们发现了我的文字，对每一个字都深信不疑。

column5: Howl scoffs, as anger boils within him.{w}\nBut before he can do anything, Pro interrupts.
column6: 豪尔嗤笑一声，怒火在胸中翻涌。{w}\n但他还没来得及做什么，普洛就打断了他。

column5: Algus Veilleur...
column6: 阿尔古斯·维勒尔……

column5: The man's ears perk up, in a way that reveals he was reacting to his name.
column6: 那人竖起了耳朵，那反应说明他是在对自己的名字有所触动。

column5: That is the moniker I assumed, yes.\nI'm happy to know that the name is still remembered.
column6: 那正是我用的名号，没错。\n我很高兴这个名字仍被人记得。

column5: Algus Veilleur...{w}\nThe man revered as the greatest historian.{w}\nI can't believe that he too, was a tool of The Triumvirate.
column6: 阿尔古斯·维勒尔……{w}\n那个被尊为史上最伟大的历史学家的人。{w}\n我简直不敢相信，他也是三人执政团的工具。

column5: I'm a bit confused, since I'm unfamiliar with the name.{w}\nBut Valinorth was very independent, so I'm not surprised.{w}\nEverybody seems a bit shocked at learning his true name.
column6: 我有些困惑，因为我对这个名字很陌生。{w}\n但瓦利诺斯一向很独立，所以我并不意外。{w}\n得知他的真名，大家似乎都有些震惊。

column5: So everything the people believe is a lie that you created?\nWhy would you need to go to such extremes...? This is insane.
column6: 所以人民所信奉的一切，都是你编造的谎言？\n你何必做到这种地步……？这太疯狂了。

column5: Look at how you and your friends reacted to learning the truth.\nIt brought you here, prepared to kill those who gave you life.\nThe people must never know the true cost of their creation.
column6: 看看你和你朋友得知真相后的反应吧。\n它把你们引到了这里，准备好去杀死那些赋予你们生命的人。\n人民绝不能知道他们被创造出来的真正代价。

column5: I don't believe this.\nHowl, get him out of our sight.
column6: 我不信。\n豪尔，把他带下去，别让他出现在我们眼前。

column5: Howl drags Algus away, as the rest of us group together.
column6: 豪尔把阿尔古斯拖走，我们其余人则聚到一起。

column5: Well, at least he didn't put up much of a fight.\nI'd like to say that I'm shocked — but I don't feel surprised at all.\nThis journey has been full of revelations. This is just another for the pile.
column6: 至少他没怎么抵抗。\n我真想说我很震惊——可我一点都不觉得意外。\n这趟旅程充满了真相。这不过是又一个而已。

column5: It doesn't really change much at all. We still have a plan.\nBut it'd be stupid to attack the enemy in the middle of the night.\nLet's rest until the break of dawn, and meet in front of the Library.
column6: 这其实改变不了什么。我们仍然有计划。\n但半夜去袭击敌人是愚蠢的。\n我们休息到破晓，然后在图书馆前会合。

column5: Remember that we're safe as long as we stay in here.\nHopefully the rest of our forces aren't too far behind.\nYou're all dismissed. See you in the morning, okay?
column6: 记住，只要待在这里面，我们就是安全的。\n希望我们其余的部队也别落后太多。\n解散吧。早上见，好吗？

column5: Where are we supposed to rest...?
column6: 我们该在哪儿休息……？

column5: I'm sure there's Private Quarters around here somewhere.\nAnd if you can't sleep, at least there's a lot of books to read.\nAfter the war, we should give this knowledge back to the people.
column6: 这附近肯定有私人寝室。\n就算睡不着，至少还有那么多书可读。\n战争结束后，我们应该把这些知识还给人民。

column5: Yeah, I agree. The Triumvirate can't hide this stuff forever.\nWe finally have proof that nobody can deny. This is amazing.\nIf we show them this, they'll accept our rule without question.
column6: 是啊，我同意。三人执政团不可能永远藏住这些东西。\n我们终于有了无人能否认的证据。太棒了。\n只要给他们看这个，他们就会毫无异议地接受我们的统治。

column5: Damek smiles, his spirits seemingly lifted.
column6: 达梅克笑了，精神似乎振作了起来。

column5: Yeah. Let's hope you're right.\nHave a good night. All of you.
column6: 是啊。但愿你说得对。\n晚安。你们所有人。

column5: With that, we're all left on our own.{w}\nPeople scatter about, reading books and exploring the Library.{w}\nI decide to look for a private room, so I can relax and gather my bearings.
column6: 说完这些，我们就各自散了。{w}\n人们四处散开，读书、探索图书馆。{w}\n我决定去找间私人房间，好放松下来，理清思路。

column5: Halin returns to the chambers of The Triumvirate.{w}\nNoticing the absence of Shane, they're a bit confused.{w}\nThey don't assume the worst, and ask Halin to brief them.
column6: 哈林回到三人执政团的议事厅。{w}\n发现肖恩不在，他们有些困惑。{w}\n他们没有往最坏处想，而是让哈林向他们汇报。

column5: Shane stayed behind to lead the naval attack.\nHe plans to trim their forces as much as possible.\nLike you anticipated — they're arriving by sea.
column6: 肖恩留下来指挥海上进攻。\n他打算尽可能地削减他们的兵力。\n正如你所预料的——他们是从海路来的。

column5: Good. Then things are going according to plan.\nWe'll have you wait in the atrium for their arrival.\nThis means that you'll be our last line of defense.
column6: 很好。那么一切正按计划进行。\n我们会让你在中庭等候他们的到来。\n也就是说，你将是我们的最后一道防线。

column5: I consider it an honor.\nBut I have to say — I'm worried for Shane.\nHis chances of survival are pretty slim out there.
column6: 我视此为荣耀。\n但我得说——我很担心肖恩。\n他在外面的生还几率相当渺茫。

column5: He knew what he was signing up for.\nIf he killed even one of the rebels, then he was successful.\nFocus on protecting this castle, Halin. That's more important.
column6: 他很清楚自己承担的是什么。\n哪怕他只杀了一个反抗军，那就算成功了。\n专心守住这座城堡，哈林。那才更重要。

column5: Yes, of course.\nI'll make sure no one passes the atrium.\nIf they try, they'll fall as quickly as they enter.
column6: 是，当然。\n我保证没人能通过中庭。\n他们若敢尝试，一进来就会倒下。

column5: Thank you, Halin.\nIt's important that they have a false sense of security.\nDon't give them too much resistance until it's absolutely necessary.
column6: 谢谢你，哈林。\n重要的是让他们产生虚假的安全感。\n在绝对必要之前，不要给他们太多阻力。

column5: If they think they're going to win, they're more prone to slipping up.\nIt's up to you to figure out when that moment is, and take advantage of it.\nEven if it takes your life, you are to prevent them from entering our chambers.
column6: 如果他们以为自己会赢，就更容易露出破绽。\n什么时候是那个时机，要由你来判断并加以利用。\n哪怕要付出你的性命，你也必须阻止他们进入我们的议事厅。

column5: Halin kneels, complying without hesitation.
column6: 哈林跪下，毫不犹豫地服从了。

column5: Yes, of course. My life for The Triumvirate.\nI'll fortify straight away, and wait for their arrival.
column6: 是，当然。我的命属于三人执政团。\n我这就去加固防备，等候他们的到来。

column5: Halin strides out of their chambers, with a sense of purpose.{w}\nAfter he leaves, they turn to each other, displaying soft smiles.
column6: 哈林带着一股决然之意，大步走出议事厅。{w}\n他离开后，他们转向彼此，露出淡淡的微笑。

column5: Hopefully this time, things will be different.
column6: 但愿这一次，事情会有所不同。

column5: After finding a private room, I pace around it in circles.{w}\nI've had nothing but bad luck when it came to getting rest.{w}\nEver since we left Mazeo, I've been too worried to fall asleep.
column6: 找到一间私人房间后，我在里面来回踱步。{w}\n说到休息，我最近就没走过好运。{w}\n自从离开马泽奥以来，我一直忧心忡忡，无法入睡。

column5: I try reading books, but none of them are able to capture my interest.{w}\nPacing the room, I basically succumb to the anxiety assaulting my mind.{w}\nHowever — and thankfully — a knock at my door soon returns me to lucidity.
column6: 我试着读书，但没有一本能引起我的兴趣。{w}\n在房间里踱着步，我几乎被侵袭心头的焦虑压垮。{w}\n然而——幸好——一阵敲门声很快让我回过神来。

column5: As soon as I open it, Howl enters.{w}\nHe takes a deep breath, sounding both annoyed and relieved.{w}\nI don't blame him, he's gone through so much in such a short time.
column6: 我一开门，豪尔就走了进来。{w}\n他深吸一口气，听起来既烦恼又宽慰。{w}\n我不怪他，这么短的时间里他经历了太多。

column5: We finally put the Librarian to rest.\nAlgus, right? He certainly likes to talk a lot.\nAnswers in the form of riddles. He simply stalls for time.
column6: 我们终于把那个图书管理员安置好了。\n阿尔古斯，对吧？他确实话很多。\n答案都是谜语。他只是在拖延时间。

column5: It is rather peculiar however, that he didn't resist.\nHe won't help us kill The Triumvirate, but he won't stop us, either.\nAs we locked him up, he mentioned his true allegiance was to history.
column6: 不过，奇怪的是他没有抵抗。\n他不会帮我们杀三人执政团，但也不会阻止我们。\n我们把他关起来时，他说自己真正的效忠对象是历史。

column5: Whether we win or lose, it will still be his job to write about the aftermath.\nSo no matter what happens, there will be a new history to record.\nAn interesting habit. Living through others, rather than yourself.
column6: 无论我们输赢，书写余波仍然是他的职责。\n所以不管发生什么，都会有一段新的历史需要记载。\n有趣的癖好。活在他人之中，而非自己之中。

column5: He looks around the room, a hint of sadness on his face.
column6: 他环顾房间，脸上带着一丝悲伤。

column5: There must not be much else to do, in such a lonely place.\nWe feel sorry for him, but there is really nothing we can do.\nHe gave us shelter, in exchange for silence.
column6: 在这样寂寞的地方，想必也没什么别的事可做。\n我们为他感到难过，但实在无能为力。\n他给了我们栖身之所，换取我们的沉默。

column5: I ask Howl how we know if we can trust him or not.
column6: 我问豪尔，我们怎么知道能不能信任他。

column5: We don't, but it does not matter.\nHe is locked up, and unable to contact anybody outside.\nAny chance he had to intervene has already passed on.
column6: 我们不知道，但这无关紧要。\n他被关起来了，无法与外界任何人联络。\n他任何介入的机会都已经过去了。

column5: Our foothold is established.\nWe've successfully taken Baltean soil, [firstname].\nWhile not our main goal, this is a major victory for all of us.
column6: 我们的据点已经建立。\n我们成功踏上了巴尔泰的土地，[firstname]。\n虽然这不是我们的主要目标，但这对我们所有人来说都是一场重大的胜利。

column5: I nod. He's right — nobody else in history has gotten this far.{w}\nWe stood a real chance at winning here, and it felt amazing.{w}\nI thank him for the status report, and for checking up on me.
column6: 我点头。他说得对——历史上从没有别人走到这一步。{w}\n我们真的有获胜的机会，那感觉太棒了。{w}\n我感谢他的情况汇报，也感谢他来看望我。

column5: Of course. We wanted to make sure you were comfortable.\nWe can imagine that rest is hard to find under these circumstances.\nMight we suggest spending some time with your friends before the dawn?
column6: 当然。我们想确认你一切安好。\n在这种情形下，想必很难得到休息。\n是否建议你在黎明前和朋友们待一会儿？

column5: As soon as I open it, Damek enters.{w}\nHe takes a deep breath, sounding both annoyed and relieved.{w}\nI don't blame him, he's gone through so much in such a short time.
column6: 我一开门，达梅克就走了进来。{w}\n他深吸一口气，听起来既烦恼又宽慰。{w}\n我不怪他，这么短的时间里他经历了太多。

column5: We finally put the Librarian to rest.\nHe sure likes to talk a lot — and about nothing at all.\nLots of answers in the form of riddles. Boring stuff.
column6: 我们终于把那个图书管理员安置好了。\n他确实很爱说话——而且尽说些没用的。\n很多答案都是谜语。无聊得很。

column5: It's pretty interesting that he didn't resist, though.\nHe said he won't help us, but he won't stop us either.\nHis true allegiance is to history. That's what he kept saying.
column6: 不过，他没抵抗倒是挺有意思的。\n他说不会帮我们，但也不会阻止我们。\n他真正的效忠对象是历史。他一直这么说。

column5: Doesn't make much sense, since he faked so much history in the past.\nBut no matter what happens next, he'll have a lot to write about.\nIf we win, he'll record it. If we lose, then he'll record that too.
column6: 这说不太通，毕竟他过去伪造了那么多历史。\n但无论接下来发生什么，他都有很多可写。\n我们赢了，他会记下来。我们输了，他也会记下来。

column5: I guess his stance makes more sense if you look at it that way.{w}\nNo matter what happens next, somebody would need to write about it.
column6: 这么一想，他的立场倒更说得通了。{w}\n无论接下来发生什么，总得有人把它写下来。

column5: His main condition was that we don't harm the Library.\nPretty good terms, especially in exchange for a foothold.\nWe may not have won yet, but we've seized Baltean soil.
column6: 他的主要条件是我们不破坏图书馆。\n条件相当不错，尤其是用在一个据点上。\n我们也许还没赢，但我们已经夺取了巴尔泰的土地。

column5: That's true. Nobody else has ever gotten this far.{w}\nI can tell that we stand a chance at winning, and it feels amazing.{w}\nBut I have to ask, how do we know that this Algus can be trusted?
column6: 没错。从没有别人走到这一步。{w}\n我能感觉到我们有机会赢，那感觉太棒了。{w}\n但我不得不问，我们怎么知道这个阿尔古斯可以信任？

column5: We don't. But he can't do much if he's locked up.\nAny chance he had at intervening is long gone, by now.\nHe can try when we leave, but we'll be prepared to fight by then.
column6: 我们不知道。但他被关着，也做不了什么。\n他任何介入的机会现在早就没了。\n我们离开时他大可以试试，但到那时我们已经做好战斗准备了。

column5: I nod, thanking Damek for the update on what's going on.
column6: 我点头，感谢达梅克告知近况。

column5: Of course. I just wanted to make sure you were alright.\nIt must be hard to sleep right now, given all the weight on your shoulders.\nThe others aren't sleeping either. Maybe you should spend some time with them?
column6: 当然。我只是想确认你没事。\n如今你肩上担子这么重，肯定很难入睡。\n其他人也都没睡。也许你该去陪陪他们？

column5: He's right. If I can't sleep, then that's probably the next best idea.{w}\nBut I wonder if our bonds are strong enough to warrant some time together.{w}\nThis could be our last night alive, after all. They might be more protective of their time.
column6: 他说得对。既然睡不着，那大概就是下一个最好的选择。{w}\n但我不知道我们的情谊是否深厚到值得共度时光。{w}\n毕竟，这可能是我们活着的最后一晚。他们也许更珍惜自己的时间。

column5: I guess there was no harm in checking. I see him out of my room, with a new goal in mind.{w}\nTurning back to face the vast emptiness of this private room, I wonder who I could invite over.{w}\nThis would be a good night to make some final memories. Just in case the worst came to pass.
column6: 去问问也无妨。我送他出了房间，心里有了新的打算。{w}\n回过头，面对这间空荡荡的私人房间，我琢磨着能邀请谁过来。{w}\n今晚是个留下最后回忆的好机会。以防最坏的情况发生。

column5: I descend the stairs of The Grand Library, the crisp Baltean air assaulting me.{w}\nI shiver, and stand in disbelief at how uninviting this city seems to be.{w}\nIf this is where I'd sit in the throne, we'd need to change a lot.
column6: 我走下大图书馆的台阶，清冷的巴尔泰空气扑面而来。{w}\n我打了个寒颤，难以置信这座城市竟如此拒人于千里之外。{w}\n如果我将来要坐上这里的王座，我们得改变很多。

column5: Looking around the area, It appears that everybody is here.{w}\nI try to take a head count, just to make sure that's correct.{w}\nThis was the final attack. We needed all of our might.
column6: 环顾四周，看来所有人都到了。{w}\n我试着清点人数，确认一下没错。{w}\n这是最后的进攻。我们需要倾尽全力。

column5: I see Damek shaking hands with the Created Seers.{w}\nGood. They helped us secure the library — and survived.{w}\nThey would be a valuable asset in holding the Town Square.
column6: 我看见达梅克在和被造先知们握手。{w}\n很好。他们帮我们拿下了图书馆——而且活了下来。{w}\n守住城镇广场，他们会是宝贵的战力。

column5: It was nice to see their full potential finally realized.{w}\nUsing their visions, they outsmarted an entire horde of enemies.{w}\nIt was in this exact moment — that I knew I made the right choice.
column6: 看到他们的全部潜能终于得以发挥，真是太好了。{w}\n他们凭借预视，智胜了整整一大群敌人。{w}\n就在这一刻——我知道自己做出了正确的选择。

column5: One fact stands out to me. The Created Seers are nowhere to be seen.{w}\nThey weren't inside the building either. This means that they had fallen.{w}\nTheir sacrifice led us to safety in The Library, though. They had won.
column6: 有一点格外刺眼。被造先知们不见踪影。{w}\n他们也不在建筑里面。这意味着他们倒下了。{w}\n不过，是他们的牺牲让我们安全抵达了图书馆。他们赢了。

column5: I find myself frightened by the thought. The Seers could see almost all outcomes.{w}\nPerhaps The Triumvirate's desires for \"quantity\" ended up in their favor, after all.{w}\nIf there were enough soldiers, then not even a Seer could cover every angle.
column6: 这个念头让我感到恐惧。先知们几乎能看见所有结果。{w}\n也许三人执政团对“数量”的执念终究还是起了作用。{w}\n只要有足够多的士兵，就连先知也无法面面俱到。

column5: I see Damek shaking hands with the Monarch Vessels.{w}\nGood. They helped us secure victory — and survived.{w}\nThey would be a valuable asset in holding the Town Square.
column6: 我看见达梅克在和君主容器们握手。{w}\n很好。他们帮我们赢得了胜利——而且活了下来。{w}\n守住城镇广场，他们会是宝贵的战力。

column5: It was nice to see their full potential finally realized.{w}\nWith their incredible resilience, they outsmarted an enemy horde.{w}\nIt was in this exact moment — that I knew I made the right choice.
column6: 看到他们的全部潜能终于得以发挥，真是太好了。{w}\n凭着惊人的韧性，他们智胜了一整群敌人。{w}\n就在这一刻——我知道自己做出了正确的选择。

column5: One fact stands out to me. The Monarch Vessels are nowhere to be seen.{w}\nThey weren't inside the building either. This means that they had fallen.{w}\nTheir sacrifice led us to safety in The Library, though. They had won.
column6: 有一点格外刺眼。君主容器们不见踪影。{w}\n他们也不在建筑里面。这意味着他们倒下了。{w}\n不过，是他们的牺牲让我们安全抵达了图书馆。他们赢了。

column5: A bit of anxiety wells up within me though. How could they have died?{w}\nIt's a frightening thought — that The Honor Guard could kill near-immortals.{w}\nMaybe The Triumvirate's desires for \"quantity\" actually ended in their favor.
column6: 不过，一丝焦虑在我心中涌起。他们怎么会死？{w}\n这是个可怕的念头——荣誉卫队竟能杀死近乎不死的存在。{w}\n也许三人执政团对“数量”的执念真的奏效了。

column5: When I make it to the bottom of the stairs, Damek waves me over.{w}\nOur forces run around, seemingly taking on an infinite number of tasks.{w}\nEverybody is doing something. It made everything seem more \"final\".
column6: 我走到台阶底部时，达梅克朝我招手。{w}\n我们的部队四处奔走，仿佛有永远做不完的事。{w}\n每个人都在忙。这让一切都显得更加“最终”。

column5: I could tell that this was the last time I'd see a lot of these people.{w}\nThere was no way we'd make it through this without any casualties.{w}\nTrying to tune out the final preparations, I make my way to Damek.
column6: 我能看出，这会是很多人我最后一次见到他们。{w}\n我们不可能毫发无伤地挺过这一切。{w}\n我努力不去理会最后的准备，走向达梅克。

column5: Good to see you, [firstname].\nI'm afraid there isn't much time to talk.\nWe can't deny it. The attack has begun.
column6: 见到你真好，[firstname]。\n恐怕没多少时间说话了。\n我们无法否认。进攻已经开始了。

column5: The Honor Guard should realize that we're here momentarily.\nAfter that, this area, and the Town Square, will be a war zone.\nAnybody who has an objective elsewhere, should be leaving.
column6: 荣誉卫队很快就会察觉到我们在这里。\n之后，这一带和城镇广场都会变成战场。\n有别的任务在身的人，该出发了。

column5: Just as he says that, Pro walks by.{w}\nDamek calls out his name, and he quickly runs over.{w}\nThat's right. He was tasked with causing a distraction in the castle.
column6: 他话音刚落，普洛正好走过。{w}\n达梅克喊了他的名字，他很快跑了过来。{w}\n对了。他的任务是在城堡里制造混乱。

column5: Hey Damek, I was just about to leave.
column6: 嘿，达梅克，我正要走了。

column5: With Gryz too, I presume?
column6: 我猜格瑞兹也一起？

column5: And you have everything you need?
column6: 你需要的东西都齐了吗？

column5: Yes, of course!\nYou know me — I'd never forget anything.\nYou're in for the distraction of a lifetime, [firstname].
column6: 当然！\n你了解我——我从不落下任何东西。\n你将看到一生难忘的精彩混乱，[firstname]。

column5: He smirks at me. A confident, cocky smirk.{w}\nIf he followed through, then I'd find no resistance.{w}\nIt should be smooth sailing when we get to the castle.
column6: 他朝我得意地一笑。那是一种自信而张狂的坏笑。{w}\n只要他做到，我就不会遇到什么阻力。{w}\n我们到城堡时应该会一帆风顺。

column5: Hey, Pro.\nBefore you go...
column6: 嘿，普洛。\n在你走之前……

column5: He holds out his hand, and it trembles softly.
column6: 他伸出手，手微微颤抖着。

column5: It's been an honor serving with you.\nI hope I see you again after this is over.
column6: 能与你共事是我的荣幸。\n希望这一切结束后我还能再见到你。

column5: He shakes Damek's hand, with a firm grip.
column6: 他握住达梅克的手，握得很紧。

column5: Trust me — the pleasure has been all mine.\nAnd I don't plan on dying. Too much writing to do.
column6: 相信我——是我的荣幸才对。\n而且我可没打算死。还有太多东西要写。

column5: The handshake is broken, and they give each other uneasy smiles.{w}\nThe kind of smile that acknowledges they may never see each other again.{w}\nAnd soon after that, Pro is on his way. Off to face his fate directly, and unafraid.
column6: 两人松开手，彼此露出不安的微笑。{w}\n那种承认彼此也许再也见不到面的笑。{w}\n不久之后，普洛就上路了。径直去面对自己的命运，毫无畏惧。

column5: I guess you should get going too, [firstname].\nDon't worry, I have more protection than I'll ever need.\nOur Rebel Forces, the Created Seers, {i}and{/i} the Draconic Army.
column6: 我想你也该出发了，[firstname]。\n别担心，我有的保护远超所需。\n我们的反抗军、被造先知，{i}还有{/i}龙族军队。

column5: No matter what they throw at us, we'll be able to handle it.\nThe true deciding factor in all of this — is you, and that blade.\nBe careful, rely on your comrades, and you'll win this for sure.
column6: 无论他们向我们抛出什么，我们都能应付。\n这一切真正的决定因素——是你，和那把剑。\n小心行事，依靠你的同伴，你一定能赢。

column5: I guess you should get going too, [firstname].\nDon't worry, I have more protection than I'll ever need.\nAll of our Rebel forces, {i}and{/i} the might of the Draconic Army.
column6: 我想你也该出发了，[firstname]。\n别担心，我有的保护远超所需。\n我们所有的反抗军，{i}还有{/i}龙族军队的威势。

column5: No matter what they throw at us, we'll be able to handle it.\nThe true deciding factor in all of this — is you, and that blade.\nBe careful, rely on your comrades, and you'll win this for sure.

column6: 无论他们向我们抛出什么，我们都能应付。\n这一切真正的决定因素——是你，和那把剑。\n小心行事，依靠你的同伴，你一定能赢。

column5: He places a hand on my shoulder.
column6: 他把一只手搭在我肩上。

column5: I know you can do this.\nNow, we just need to cause a distraction.\nAll of those suits should be focusing on {i}me{/i}.
column6: 我知道你能做到。\n现在，我们只需要制造混乱。\n那些盔甲全都该把注意力放在{i}我{/i}身上。

column5: If all goes as planned, you should find minimal resistance.\nSave your strength for The Triumvirate. I think you'll need it.\nAnyway — don't worry about me, I'll have Howl by my side.
column6: 如果一切按计划进行，你应该不会遇到多少阻力。\n把力气留给三人执政团。我觉得你会用得上的。\n总之——别担心我，豪尔会在我身边。

column5: He looks around, confusion worn on his face.
column6: 他环顾四周，脸上写满困惑。

column5: Speaking of which — where {i}is{/i} he...?\nHe should've been out here ages ago.
column6: 说到这个——他{i}人{/i}呢……？\n他早该出来了。

column5: Before I can even respond, I hear a loud cracking noise.{w}\nTurning to see the source, I see the door to the Library smashed open.{w}\nAlgus is shoved through, landing face-first on the stone, still tied up.
column6: 我还没来得及回答，就听见一声巨响的破裂声。{w}\n转头看去，只见图书馆的大门被撞开了。{w}\n阿尔古斯被推了出来，脸朝下摔在石地上，仍被捆着。

column5: Smoke billows out of the open door as Howl exits The Library.{w}\nAlgus struggles on the ground, squirming like some sort of insect.{w}\nA blaze, as bright as the sun itself, makes Howl look like a silhouette.
column6: 豪尔走出图书馆时，浓烟从敞开的门里翻涌而出。{w}\n阿尔古斯在地上挣扎，像只虫子一样扭动。{w}\n一团亮如太阳的火焰，让豪尔看起来如同一道剪影。

column5: Howl...? What are you doing!?
column6: 豪尔……？你在干什么！？

column5: Upon hearing Damek, he steps forward, and grips Algus by the hair.{w}\nRaising him to his knees, he looks down in horror at our massive army.{w}\nIt was almost, as if, in that moment — he knew he was on the wrong side.
column6: 听到达梅克的声音，他上前一步，抓住阿尔古斯的头发。{w}\n把他拽得跪起来，让他惊恐地俯视我们庞大的军队。{w}\n那一刻，他几乎像是——明白了自己站错了边。

column5: We've come here to destroy The Triumvirate, and all that they stand for.\nDon't tell us you're backing down, now that the moment is upon us...?
column6: 我们来这里，是为了摧毁三人执政团，以及他们所代表的一切。\n你不会是想说，到了这一刻你反而要退缩吧……？

column5: We all stare in awe as Howl pulls out a dagger, holding it in his free hand.{w}\nThe smoke, and the bright illumination reveal to us one frightening fact.{w}\nHowl had torched the inside, burning the books — and his culture.
column6: 我们全都惊愕地看着豪尔抽出一把匕首，握在空着的那只手里。{w}\n浓烟与明亮的火光向我们揭示了一个可怕的事实。{w}\n豪尔点燃了图书馆内部，烧掉了那些书——以及他的文化。

column5: No — of course not...!\nI would never give up when we're so close.\nCome down here Howl. Explain yourself!
column6: 不——当然不是……！\n我们如此接近，我绝不会放弃。\n下来，豪尔。给我解释清楚！

column5: Howl shakes his head, disobeying Damek's order.{w}\nRunning the dagger along Algus' throat, he then kicks him down the stairs.{w}\nA trail of blood follows him all the way down, steaming against the cold snow.
column6: 豪尔摇了摇头，违抗了达梅克的命令。{w}\n他用匕首划过阿尔古斯的喉咙，然后一脚把他踹下台阶。{w}\n一道血迹一路尾随他向下，在冰冷的雪地上冒着热气。

column5: The Monarchy is dead, Damek.\nDo not cling to memories like us.
column6: 王朝已经死了，达梅克。\n别像我们这样抓着回忆不放。

column5: He slowly descends the stairs, the crimson dagger dripping blood.{w}\nAs the flames shoot out the front door, Howl's face is finally lit up.{w}\nIt appears devoid of all feeling, even after what he had done.
column6: 他缓缓走下台阶，那把绯红的匕首滴着血。{w}\n火焰从前门喷涌而出，豪尔的脸终于被照亮。{w}\n即便刚做了那样的事，那张脸上却毫无表情。

column5: Howl — stand down...!
column6: 豪尔——住手……！

column5: Damek immediately draws his sword, holding it toward Howl.
column6: 达梅克立刻拔剑，指向豪尔。

column5: Stand down? All we've done is carry out our orders.\nKill The Triumvirate, and their supporters, correct?\nAs their servant, Algus deserves the same fate.
column6: 住手？我们所做的不过是执行命令。\n杀掉三人执政团，以及他们的支持者，对吧？\n作为他们的仆从，阿尔古斯活该有同样的下场。

column5: Damek's arm trembles, realizing Howl was right.
column6: 达梅克的手臂颤抖着，意识到豪尔说得没错。

column5: And we needed a beacon to lure The Honor Guard to the square.\nA beacon — that no matter how hard they try — they cannot put out.\nBurning The Library made sense. They are not permitted inside.
column6: 而且我们需要一个灯塔，把荣誉卫队引到广场来。\n一个灯塔——无论他们怎么努力，都无法扑灭。\n烧掉图书馆是合理的。他们不被允许进入里面。

column5: Do not mourn for what has already been lost, Damek.\nThe Honor Guard will be here in just a few moments.\nPreparing your army would be a much better action.
column6: 别为已经失去的东西哀悼，达梅克。\n荣誉卫队马上就会到了。\n去准备好你的军队才是更该做的事。

column5: Howl throws the dagger onto the ground.
column6: 豪尔把匕首扔到地上。

column5: The battle for Alestia has begun.
column6: 阿拉斯蒂亚之战已经打响。

column5: Damek lowers his sword, letting out a loud sigh.{w}\nHowl was right. Algus served the enemy — making him an enemy.{w}\nAnd the beacon was paramount to our success. It could {i}not{/i} be put out.
column6: 达梅克放下剑，长叹一声。{w}\n豪尔说得对。阿尔古斯为敌人效力——那他就是敌人。{w}\n而那座灯塔对我们的成功至关重要。它{i}绝不能{/i}被扑灭。

column5: I don't believe this...
column6: 我真不敢相信……

column5: Howl finally makes it to our location, and stands beside us.{w}\nHe shrugs — almost like this isn't a big deal at all.
column6: 豪尔终于来到我们所在的位置，站在我们身旁。{w}\n他耸耸肩——仿佛这根本算不了什么。

column5: Drastic measures must be taken in order to ensure our victory.\nThe writing of a long dead culture is a small price to pay.\nYou should be on your way, [firstname]. The time is now.
column6: 为了确保胜利，必须采取极端手段。\n一个早已消亡的文化的文字，只是小小的代价。\n你该出发了，[firstname]。就是现在。

column5: He's right. I had to make my way to the castle.{w}\nIf I used the Mountain Pass, I should find little resistance.{w}\nEvery suit of armor would soon be on their way to The Library.
column6: 他说得对。我得赶往城堡。{w}\n如果我走山道，应该不会遇到多少阻力。{w}\n所有盔甲很快就会赶去图书馆。

column5: Do not forget Sovy, either.\nHe volunteered to accompany your group.\nMake use of the knowledge he has on Balteus.
column6: 也别忘记索维。\n他自愿随你们这一组同行。\n好好利用他对巴尔泰乌斯的了解。

column5: Do not forget your comrades, either.\nThe success of your group will determine everything.\nDo not waver. Do not falter. Your rule hangs in the balance.
column6: 也别忘记你的同伴们。\n你们这一组的成败将决定一切。\n不要动摇。不要迟疑。你的统治悬于一线。

column5: I nod. This was happening so fast, but I could waste no time.{w}\nWe knew this was coming. We knew we'd have to take action.{w}\nI start to walk away, but Damek calls out to me a moment later.
column6: 我点头。这一切发生得太快，但我一刻也不能浪费。{w}\n我们知道这终将到来。我们知道必须采取行动。{w}\n我转身要走，但片刻后达梅克叫住了我。

column5: Hey — be careful, okay...?\nI want to see you there when we regroup in the atrium.\nAnd if all goes as planned, you'll be seeing {i}me{/i} there, too.
column6: 嘿——小心点，好吗……？\n等我们在中庭会合时，我想看到你也在那儿。\n如果一切顺利，你也会在那儿见到{i}我{/i}。

column5: I smile, and nod. That would have to suffice as a goodbye.{w}\nAfter I gather up Valessa, Ulric, Fortaime and Sovy, we head out.{w}\nIf we hurried, we could get through the Town Square before the suits came.
column6: 我笑着点头。这就当作告别吧。{w}\n我召集了瓦莱莎、乌尔里克、福泰姆和索维，我们一起出发。{w}\n如果抓紧时间，我们能在那些盔甲赶来前穿过城镇广场。

column5: I smile, and nod. That would have to suffice as a goodbye.{w}\nAfter I gather up Valessa, Ulric and Fortaime — we decide to head out.{w}\nIf we hurried, we could get through the Town Square before the suits came.
column6: 我笑着点头。这就当作告别吧。{w}\n我召集了瓦莱莎、乌尔里克和福泰姆——我们决定出发。{w}\n如果抓紧时间，我们能在那些盔甲赶来前穿过城镇广场。

column5: In our haste, we say almost no words to one another.{w}\nThere was a silent agreement that the task at hand was more important.{w}\nIn knowing that any word could be our last — silence seemed more appropriate.
column6: 匆匆之间，我们几乎谁也没对谁说话。{w}\n彼此心照不宣：眼前的要紧事更重要。{w}\n知道任何一句话都可能是最后一句话——沉默反而更合适。

column5: Halin knelt before his Masters, more eager to serve than he had ever been before.{w}\nHe looked up at them, awaiting their orders. Perhaps the final orders they'd give.{w}\nIt would be up to him to lead The Honor Guard, and ensure their victory today.
column6: 哈林跪在主人面前，从没有像此刻这样渴望效命。{w}\n他抬头望向他们，等待命令。也许是他们下的最后命令。{w}\n指挥荣誉卫队、确保他们今日取胜的重任，将落在他肩上。

column5: Rise, Halin.\nIt seems they seek to deceive us.\nBut it's nothing we haven't seen before.
column6: 起来吧，哈林。\n看来他们想欺骗我们。\n但这我们见多了。

column5: Deception...?\nThat seems to be their strength.\nWhat will you have me do, Masters?
column6: 欺骗……？\n那似乎正是他们的强项。\n主人，您要我怎么做？

column5: Man the atrium. Stay in the castle.\nWe shall let them exhaust their forces for now.\nWhen they come here, you can finish them off.
column6: 守住中庭。留在城堡里。\n暂且让他们耗尽兵力。\n等他们来到这里，你就可以将他们一网打尽。

column5: You mean to fall into their trap...?
column6: 您是说，要落入他们的陷阱……？

column5: Doing so would make it {i}our{/i} trap, Halin.\nBesides, their deaths will feed the blade even more.\nWe need it as strong as possible when it is brought back to us.
column6: 那样一来，那就会变成{i}我们的{/i}陷阱，哈林。\n再说，他们的死会让那把剑变得更加强大。\n当它被带回我们手中时，我们需要它尽可能地强。

column5: For what reason?
column6: 为了什么？

column5: Do you doubt us...?
column6: 你在怀疑我们……？

column5: No, of course not.\nI was merely curious — that's all.
column6: 不，当然不是。\n我只是好奇——仅此而已。

column5: Then your curiosity will have to linger.\nYou have your orders, Halin. Now see them out.\nIn a few hours, everything should be over for good.
column6: 那你的好奇心就只能搁着了。\n命令已经下达，哈林。去执行吧。\n几个小时后，一切都该彻底结束了。

column5: Halin wondered — but for what side...?
column6: 哈林心中暗自揣测——可究竟是哪一方会终结呢……？

column5: Yes — whatever you say.\nWhen they arrive in the atrium? Consider them dead.\nI will paint the walls with their blood, or else besmirch them with my own.
column6: 是——您怎么说都行。\n等他们来到中庭？就当他们已经死了。\n我要用他们的血涂满墙壁，否则就用我自己的血来玷污它。

column5: Thank you Halin. Now be on your way.\nWe will send The Honor Guard to the Town Square to weaken them.\nThere is no time to waste. The end of everything is upon us.
column6: 谢谢你，哈林。现在就出发吧。\n我们会派荣誉卫队去城镇广场削弱他们。\n没时间可浪费了。万物的终局已经降临。

column5: Without a word, Halin is off on his way.{w}\nIn this moment, he truly became The Grand Inquisitor.{w}\nLast line of defense between The Triumvirate and a weak insurrection.
column6: 哈林一言不发地上路了。{w}\n在这一刻，他真正成为了大审判官。{w}\n三人执政团与一场微弱叛乱之间的最后一道防线。

column5: The end? Or perhaps, another new beginning...\nSteel yourselves, brothers. You know what's coming.
column6: 终结？又或者，是另一个新的开始……\n振作起来，兄弟们。你们知道即将到来的是什么。

column5: They all look at each other, and nod.{w}\nFor the first time in ages, doubt fills their chambers.{w}\nThankfully, nobody was there to witness such a fault.
column6: 他们彼此对视，点了点头。{w}\n许久以来第一次，疑虑充满了他们的议事厅。{w}\n幸好，无人目睹这样的破绽。

column5: Pro and Gryz enter The Triumvirate's castle, careful not to attract attention.{w}\nThe staircase in the middle is the one that led to their chambers, for sure.{w}\nThis meant they'd have to lure The Honor Guard off to the left or right side.
column6: 普洛和格瑞兹进入三人执政团的城堡，小心不引人注意。{w}\n中间那道楼梯无疑是通往他们议事厅的。{w}\n这就意味着他们得把荣誉卫队引到左侧或右侧去。

column5: Paths on either side of the stairs lead to other sections of the castle.{w}\nIf Pro had to guess, he'd say that they led to living quarters, or practice rooms.{w}\nMuch to their luck, a horde of Honor Guard was gathered at the base of the stairs.
column6: 楼梯两侧的通道通往城堡的其他区域。{w}\n如果让普洛猜，他会说那些是通往起居室或练武场的。{w}\n幸运的是，楼梯底部聚集着一大群荣誉卫队。

column5: Alright, alright.\nHow can we lure them away...?\nThink Pro, think. You can do this!
column6: 好，好。\n我们怎样才能把他们引开……？\n想想，普洛，想想。你能行！

column5: Not so loud, Pro.\nWe need a plan {i}before{/i} they find us.\nLet's look for something we can use as a distraction.
column6: 小声点，普洛。\n我们得在被他们发现{i}之前{/i}想好计划。\n找找有什么能用来制造混乱的东西。

column5: Pro examines the area, noticing large metallic stands holding lit candles.{w}\nThat would be sure to cause a distraction. But how would he use it...?{w}\nHis eyes are drawn to large stained-glass windows lining the hall.
column6: 普洛打量着这一带，注意到几个托着点燃蜡烛的大型金属烛台。{w}\n那肯定能制造混乱。但他要怎么利用呢……？{w}\n他的目光被走廊两旁巨大的彩绘玻璃窗吸引过去。

column5: Hmm. That'll have to do.\nCome on Gryz, let's do this already.\nHopefully [firstname] isn't too far behind.
column6: 嗯。只能这样了。\n来吧格瑞兹，我们动手吧。\n希望[firstname]别落后太多。

column5: He starts moving toward the candleholders, but Gryz grabs his shoulder.
column6: 他朝烛台走去，但格瑞兹抓住了他的肩膀。

column5: No — not that side.\nIt leads to the dining hall, and a dead end.\nYou'd only be signing your own death warrant.
column6: 不——不是那边。\n那边通往餐厅，是条死路。\n你那是给自己签死亡判决书。

column5: Pro nods without a word, and they make their way to the other side of the room.{w}\nThey both grab one of the stands, and shake off the candle on the other end.{w}\nIt hits the ground, and the wax shatters in almost every possible direction.
column6: 普洛一言不发地点头，两人走向房间的另一侧。{w}\n他们各抓住一个烛台，把另一端的蜡烛抖落。{w}\n蜡烛落地，蜡几乎朝四面八方碎裂飞散。

column5: Hey — over here...!

In unison, both Pro and Gryz start breaking the windows with their \"weapons\".{w}\nThe Honor Guard takes notice immediately, and starts sauntering over.{w}\nPro grins, laughing softly at how easily it was to distract the suits.
column6: 普洛和格瑞兹同时用他们的“武器”开始砸窗。{w}\n荣誉卫队立刻注意到了，开始慢悠悠地走过来。{w}\n普洛咧嘴一笑，轻声笑着——引开那些盔甲竟这么容易。

column5: Perfect. Now we just need to make a trail.\nCome on! Don't let us get away...!
column6: 完美。现在我们只需要留下一道痕迹。\n来啊！别让我们跑了……！

column5: They run down the hallway, shattering window after window.{w}\nA trail of broken glass is left behind for the suits to follow after.{w}\nHowever, they move slow on purpose, keeping an eye on the horde.
column6: 他们沿着走廊奔跑，砸碎一扇又一扇窗户。{w}\n身后留下一道碎玻璃的痕迹，供那些盔甲循迹追来。{w}\n不过他们故意放慢脚步，留意着那群追兵。

column5: Pro enters The Triumvirate's castle, careful not to gather unwanted attention.{w}\nThe staircase in the middle is the one that led up to their chambers, for sure.{w}\nThis meant he'd have to lure The Honor Guard off to the left or right side.
column6: 普洛进入三人执政团的城堡，小心不引来不必要的注意。{w}\n中间那道楼梯无疑是通往他们议事厅的。{w}\n这就意味着他得把荣誉卫队引到左侧或右侧去。

column5: Paths on either side of the stairs lead to other sections of the castle.{w}\nIf he had to guess, he'd say that they led to living quarters, or practice rooms.{w}\nMuch to his luck, a horde of Honor Guard was gathered at the base of the stairs.
column6: 楼梯两侧的通道通往城堡的其他区域。{w}\n如果让他猜，他会说那些是通往起居室或练武场的。{w}\n幸运的是，楼梯底部聚集着一大群荣誉卫队。

column5: Alright, alright.\nHow can I lure them away...?\nThink Pro, think. You can do this.
column6: 好，好。\n我怎样才能把他们引开……？\n想想，普洛，想想。你能行。

column5: He examines the area, noticing large metallic stands holding lit candles.{w}\nThat would be sure to cause a distraction. But how would he use it...?{w}\nHis eyes are drawn to large stained-glass windows lining the hall.
column6: 他打量着这一带，注意到几个托着点燃蜡烛的大型金属烛台。{w}\n那肯定能制造混乱。但他要怎么利用呢……？{w}\n他的目光被走廊两旁巨大的彩绘玻璃窗吸引过去。

column5: Hmm. That'll have to do.\nHopefully [firstname] isn't too far away.\nI won't be able to keep them occupied forever.
column6: 嗯。只能这样了。\n希望[firstname]别离得太远。\n我可没法永远拖住他们。

column5: Pro grabs one of the metallic stands, and shakes off the candle.{w}\nIt falls to the ground, the wax shattering in almost every direction.{w}\nWasting no time, he causes as big of a commotion as he can.
column6: 普洛抓起一个金属烛台，抖落蜡烛。{w}\n蜡烛落到地上，蜡几乎朝四面八方碎裂飞散。{w}\n他一刻也不耽搁，尽可能闹出最大的动静。

column5: Hey, over here...!
column6: 嘿，这边……！

column5: He shatters one of the windows by thrusting the candleholder through it.{w}\nThe Honor Guard looks over and immediately begins walking toward Pro.{w}\nWith a quick smirk, he laughs at how easily he was able to carry out his goal.
column6: 他把烛台狠狠捅进一扇窗户，将其砸碎。{w}\n荣誉卫队看过来，立刻开始朝普洛走去。{w}\n他嘴角一挑，笑着——目标达成得竟如此轻而易举。

column5: Perfect. Now, just to make a trail.\nCome on! Don't let me get away...!
column6: 完美。现在，只要留下痕迹就行。\n来啊！别让我跑了……！

column5: He runs down the hallway, shattering window after window.{w}\nA trail of broken glass is left behind for the suits to follow after.{w}\nHowever, he moves slow on purpose, keeping an eye on the horde.
column6: 他沿着走廊奔跑，砸碎一扇又一扇窗户。{w}\n身后留下一道碎玻璃的痕迹，供那些盔甲循迹追来。{w}\n不过他是故意放慢脚步，留意着那群追兵。

column5: Howl and Damek stand side by side in the Town Square of Balteus.{w}\nThey can hear the sound of The Honor Guard marching to their location.{w}\nEchoes of steel grating against steel assault their ears as they wait.
column6: 豪尔和达梅克并肩站在巴尔泰乌斯的城镇广场上。{w}\n他们能听见荣誉卫队朝他们所在之处行进的脚步声。{w}\n等候之际，钢铁与钢铁摩擦的回响刺痛着他们的耳朵。

column5: How many do you think there are?
column6: 你觉得有多少？

column5: Not enough.
column6: 不够多。

column5: Well, at least you're confident.
column6: 好吧，至少你很有自信。

column5: Damek brushes some ash off of his shoulder.{w}\nRemnants of the books from the library filled the air.{w}\nFrom behind, one of their allies steps forward.
column6: 达梅克拂去肩上的灰烬。{w}\n图书馆那些书的残灰弥漫在空气中。{w}\n一名盟友从他们身后走上前来。

column5: They're getting close. Be on your guard, Damek.\nI'll have my men protect you and Howl.
column6: 他们快到了。提高警惕，达梅克。\n我会让我的部下保护你和豪尔。

column5: They're almost here — I can tell.\nBe on your guard. I'll have my men protect you.
column6: 他们快到了——我能感觉到。\n提高警惕。我会让我的部下保护你。

column5: Yes, of course. I appreciate it.\nI'll be watching their backs as well.
column6: 好，当然。多谢。\n我也会替他们留意背后。

column5: Now, all three of them were standing side by side.{w}\nThe footsteps of The Honor Guard got louder and louder.{w}\nThey stepped in unison, sounding like a heart that beat too fast.
column6: 现在，他们三人都并肩站在一起。{w}\n荣誉卫队的脚步声越来越响。{w}\n他们步伐一致，听起来像一颗跳动过快的心。

column5: It reminds me of the drums in the coliseum.\nBefore every fight, they'd put on quite a show.\nNothing got my blood pumping more. Trust me.
column6: 这让我想起竞技场里的鼓声。\n每场战斗前，他们都会上演一番好戏。\n再没有比这更让我热血沸腾的了。相信我。

column5: Then we trust that you'll perform admirably.\nShow us that siding with you was the right choice.\nEvery step we've ever taken — has led us to this moment.
column6: 那我们相信你会表现出色。\n向我们证明，与你结盟是正确的选择。\n我们迈出的每一步——都将我们引向这一刻。

column5: Draycu smirks.
column6: 德雷库得意地一笑。

column5: We'll give the world something to sing about.\nTrust me, they'll tell tales of this battle.
column6: 我们要给这世界一些值得传唱的东西。\n相信我，他们会传颂这场战斗的。

column5: Reminds me of those drums in the coliseum.\nEvery time they played, I knew that death would follow.\nLet's hope that it does — but not for any of us.
column6: 让我想起竞技场里的那些鼓声。\n每次鼓声响起，我就知道死亡会随之而来。\n但愿这次也一样——但不是冲着我们任何人。

column5: If we are in danger, do not come to our aid.\nEspecially if it would endanger the lives of others.\nRemember — by all accounts, we are already dead.
column6: 如果我们陷入危险，不要来救我们。\n尤其是当这会危及他人性命的时候。\n记住——从各方面来说，我们已经死了。

column5: Vivien shakes his head.
column6: 薇薇安摇了摇头。

column5: No matter what you say, you're an ally.\nAnd believe it or not — I prefer to keep those alive.\nAs long as you breathe? You're living, and of use.
column6: 不管你怎么说，你是盟友。\n信不信由你——我更喜欢让盟友活着。\n只要你还在呼吸？你就是活着的，就有用。

column5: As they talk, the first of The Honor Guard comes into view.{w}\nOne stood in front of the rest, as if assigning themselves the role of leader.{w}\nIt was odd, they all thought, that such mindless suits had a sense of hierarchy.
column6: 他们交谈间，荣誉卫队的第一个成员出现在视野中。{w}\n有一个站在其余成员前面，仿佛给自己安上了首领的角色。{w}\n他们心想，这些没脑子的盔甲居然还有等级意识，真是奇怪。

column5: However, there was no time to think about such trivial things.{w}\nMere moments later, the rest of the suits gather behind their \"leader\".{w}\nOn the other side of the town square, it seemed like thousands had arrived.
column6: 然而，已经没时间想这些琐碎的事了。{w}\n只过了片刻，其余盔甲便聚集在他们的“首领”身后。{w}\n城镇广场的另一头，仿佛来了成千上万个。

column5: It appears that we may be outnumbered.\nBut remember, those things aren't known for their smarts.\nEach one of us could easily take down a hundred or more.
column6: 看来我们寡不敌众。\n但记住，那些东西可不以聪明著称。\n我们每个人都能轻松撂倒一百个甚至更多。

column5: Let's hope that you're correct.
column6: 但愿你说得对。

column5: Damek gulps and draws his sword.{w}\nEverybody behind him does the same, and the sound fills the Town Square.{w}\nEven from the opposing side — all they can hear is the unsheathing of blades.
column6: 达梅克咽了口唾沫，拔出剑。{w}\n他身后的每个人也都照做，拔剑声充满了城镇广场。{w}\n就连对面——他们能听到的也只有拔剑声。

column5: But when everybody is armed, nothing happens.{w}\nThey stand on opposite sides, both forces staring at each other.{w}\nDamek looks left, and right, to his allies, before speaking out.
column6: 但当所有人都拿起武器后，却什么都没发生。{w}\n他们分立两侧，两军对望。{w}\n达梅克左右看了看自己的盟友，然后开口。

column5: It appears they want us to make the first move.\nProbably so they can counter. That makes it easier.\nJust anticipate it, and come up with a counter of your own.
column6: 看来他们想让我们先动手。\n多半是为了好反击。反倒更容易了。\n只要预判它，想出自己的反制就行。

column5: Even after his instruction, nobody makes a move.{w}\nThe ash in the air thickens — remnants of The Monarchy showering over them.{w}\nDamek takes a few steps forward, and holds his sword up in the air.
column6: 即便他下了指示，仍无人行动。{w}\n空气中的灰烬更浓了——王朝的残烬如雨般洒落在他们身上。{w}\n达梅克向前走了几步，把剑高举在空中。

column5: We fight to liberate those stuck under The Triumvirate's thumb.\nIn the name of all those who have fallen, and all those who will come.\nA new future will dawn here today — one of happiness and peace for all.
column6: 我们战斗，是为了解放那些受三人执政团压迫的人。\n以所有已逝者、以及所有将来者的名义。\n今天，一个崭新的未来将在这里破晓——一个属于所有人、充满幸福与和平的未来。

column5: The soldiers cheer, holding their swords up in the air as well.{w}\nBut soon after, they fall back down — resting in a fighting position.{w}\nDamek says nothing, simply holding his sword toward the enemy.
column6: 士兵们欢呼着，也把剑高举在空中。{w}\n但很快，剑又落下——摆出战斗的架势。{w}\n达梅克没有作声，只是把剑指向敌人。

column5: And that was enough to spring the army into action.{w}\nCharging toward The Honor Guard, steel soon clashes against steel.{w}\nScreams fill the Town Square as both sides meet and clash in the middle.
column6: 这就足以让整支军队行动起来。{w}\n他们冲向荣誉卫队，钢铁很快碰撞在一起。{w}\n双方在中央交锋，城镇广场上充斥着惨叫。

column5: Damek and Howl remain behind everybody, watching the initial charge.{w}\nThey'd wait for an ample opening, and join their army at the right time.{w}\nHowl places a hand on Damek's shoulder, and gives him a soft nod.
column6: 达梅克和豪尔留在所有人身后，注视着最初的冲锋。{w}\n他们要等待充足的战机，在合适的时机加入军队。{w}\n豪尔把手搭在达梅克肩上，轻轻点了点头。

column5: Damek — it is time.
column6: 达梅克——时候到了。

column5: In response, he gulps, and looks up at Howl.
column6: 他咽了口唾沫，抬头望向豪尔。

column5: Yeah. This is it.
column6: 是啊。就是现在。

column5: He catches a bunch of falling ash in his hand.{w}\nAfter looking at it for a moment, he crushes it in a fist.
column6: 他伸手接住一把飘落的灰烬。{w}\n看了一会儿后，他把它攥进拳里。

column5: Charge!
column6: 冲锋！

column5: And mere seconds later — they were lost in the crowd.
column6: 仅仅几秒后——他们就消失在人群中。

column5: We arrive at what seems to be the summit of the Mountain Pass.{w}\nThough we took the long way around, I could still hear fighting in Balteus.{w}\nSwords clashing against swords, and the screaming of agony found only in war.
column6: 我们抵达了似乎是山道的最高处。{w}\n虽然我们绕了远路，我仍能听见巴尔泰乌斯那边的厮杀。{w}\n剑与剑的碰撞，还有唯有战争中才有的痛苦惨叫。

column5: We all spread out as soon as we arrive in the same spot.{w}\nI was a bit ahead of everyone else, so I let them catch up.{w}\nWhen they do, Sovy decides to approach me for a chat.
column6: 一到同一处，我们就四下散开。{w}\n我比其他人稍稍靠前，便让他们赶上来。{w}\n等他们跟上，索维决定过来找我聊聊。

column5: We're almost there. It won't be much longer.\nAs soon as we turn the next corner, you'll see the castle.\nThis is probably the best place for Fortaime to leave our side.
column6: 我们就快到了。不会太久了。\n一转过下一个拐角，你就能看到城堡。\n这里大概就是福泰姆离队的最佳地点。

column5: I know his task is dangerous, but I'm sure he'll be fine.\nI've heard nothing but good things about his ability to climb.\nI'm more worried about what will happen to us in the castle.
column6: 我知道他的任务很危险，但我相信他会没事的。\n关于他的攀爬本领，我听到的全是好话。\n我更担心的是我们进了城堡后会怎样。

column5: I shrug. There was really no way to know.{w}\nHopefully, Pro was able to cause his distraction.
column6: 我耸耸肩。实在无从得知。{w}\n但愿普洛成功制造了混乱。

column5: I normally hate relying on others, you know.\nIn a bind, I can only really count on my own skills.\nBut you and your friends have started to change my mind.
column6: 你知道，我平时很讨厌依赖别人。\n陷入困境时，我真正能依靠的只有自己的本事。\n但你和你朋友开始改变我的想法。

column5: We're pressed for time, so I won't draw this out any longer.\nJust know that I'll have your back in there, as I'm sure you'll have mine.\nIf we make it through this unscathed, I'll know it was a team effort.
column6: 我们时间紧迫，所以我就不多说了。\n你只要知道，到里面我会护着你的后背，我相信你也会护着我。\n如果我们能毫发无伤地挺过这一关，我就知道这是大家齐心协力的结果。

column5: I nod, as Sovy turns away and starts to look around the area.{w}\nIt appears like he's been here before, and finds great comfort in it.{w}\nA few seconds later, my attention is diverted toward an ecstatic Fortaime.
column6: 我点头，索维转过身，开始打量这一带。{w}\n看来他以前来过这里，并在这里找到了极大的慰藉。{w}\n几秒后，我的注意力被欣喜若狂的福泰姆吸引过去。

column5: We all spread out as soon as we arrive in the same spot.{w}\nI was a bit ahead of everyone else, so I let them catch up.{w}\nWhen they do, Fortaime seems lost in awe at everything.
column6: 一到同一处，我们就四下散开。{w}\n我比其他人稍稍靠前，便让他们赶上来。{w}\n等他们跟上，福泰姆似乎看什么都惊叹不已。

column5: Whoa, this is so cool!\nThat statue — I've never seen anything like it.\nUlric, what is it? Do you have any idea?
column6: 哇，这太酷了！\n那座雕像——我从没见过那样的东西。\n乌尔里克，那是什么？你知道吗？

column5: Ulric turns to face the large, intimidating statue.
column6: 乌尔里克转头看向那座巨大而令人生畏的雕像。

column5: Yeah. Alestia wasn't always fully mapped out.\nThis is an artist's depiction of the draconic people.\nAt least, a depiction made in fright, during first contact.
column6: 知道。阿拉斯蒂亚并非一直都被完整描绘过。\n这是艺术家对龙族的描画。\n至少，是初次接触时出于恐惧所作的描画。

column5: First contact...?
column6: 初次接触……？

column5: Imagine being the first mainlander to arrive in Alarinthia.\nThe people there reacted with hostility, attacking almost instantly.\nHe was an unlucky man, and he fled almost as quickly as he got there.
column6: 想象一下，作为第一个抵达阿拉林西亚的大陆人。\n那里的人反应充满敌意，几乎立刻就发动了攻击。\n他是个倒霉的人，刚一到就几乎立刻逃走了。

column5: That sounds awful.
column6: 听起来太糟了。

column5: Yeah. When he got back to Mazeo, he told everyone his story.\nBut his account wasn't right. Fear can warp anything you see.\nEven when he was proven wrong, the design still stuck.
column6: 是啊。他回到马泽奥后，把自己的经历讲给所有人听。\n但他的叙述并不准确。恐惧会扭曲你所看到的一切。\n即便后来证明他错了，那个形象仍然流传了下来。

column5: They're often used to scare away potential visitors.\nSo it makes perfect sense that there'd be one in a place like this.\nIt's guarding a shortcut that leads right to The Triumvirate's home.
column6: 它们常被用来吓退潜在的访客。\n所以在这样的地方有一座，也就完全说得通了。\n它守着的是一条直通三人执政团居所的捷径。

column5: Well, it's not gonna scare {i}me{/i} away.\nI have the most important task of all.
column6: 好吧，它可吓不走{i}我{/i}。\n我肩负着最重要的任务呢。

column5: Ulric nods, as Fortaime quickly walks over toward me.{w}\nI can tell that he's frightened, but he looks hopeful as well.
column6: 乌尔里克点头，福泰姆很快朝我走来。{w}\n我能看出他害怕，但同时也满怀希望。

column5: I promise you — I'll make it through this!\nYou better be in that atrium waiting for me.\nNo way we're failing {i}now{/i}. This is the end.
column6: 我向你保证——我一定能挺过这一关！\n你最好在中庭等着我。\n我们绝不可能{i}现在{/i}失败。这是终局了。

column5: I nod, and a moment later, we're locked in a tight embrace.
column6: 我点头，片刻后，我们紧紧相拥。

column5: Never forget that I love you, [firstname].\nEven if all else seems lost — that will never change.\nWhatever happens next, we'll handle it as a team.
column6: 永远别忘了，我爱你，[firstname]。\n就算一切都似乎失去了——这一点也永远不会变。\n接下来无论发生什么，我们都作为一支队伍去面对。

column5: We kiss, perhaps, for the last time.
column6: 我们亲吻，也许，这是最后一次。

column5: I promise you — I'll make it through this!\nYou better be in that atrium waiting for me.\nNo way we're failing {i}now{/i}. This is the end.
column6: 我向你保证——我一定能挺过这一关！\n你最好在中庭等着我。\n我们绝不可能{i}现在{/i}失败。这是终局了。

column5: We give each other a quick hug. Perhaps our last hug.{w}\nHe looks around, and shakes his head with a loud sigh.
column6: 我们匆匆拥抱了一下。也许是我们最后一次拥抱。{w}\n他环顾四周，摇了摇头，长叹一声。

column5: Well, I guess I should get going.\nI need to take a different path than the rest of you.\nI'm not used to being on my own, but I'll manage.
column6: 好吧，我想我该走了。\n我得走一条和你们其他人不同的路。\n我不习惯独自一人，但我会应付得来。

column5: Before he heads out, he hugs Valessa.{w}\nThey share a few words together, and then he's off on his way.{w}\nHis path would lead to the tower, while ours would lead directly inside.
column6: 出发前，他拥抱了瓦莱莎。{w}\n他们一起说了几句话，然后他就上路了。{w}\n他的路通向那座塔楼，而我们的则直通城堡内部。

column5: I guess we should go, too.\nThe sound of all that fighting is really scaring me.\nOne side has to be winning — but which one is it...?
column6: 我想我们也该走了。\n那一片厮杀声真让我害怕。\n总有一方在赢——可到底是哪一方……？

column5: It's best not to pay it any mind. \nWe have our own task, Valessa.
column6: 最好别去理会它。\n我们有我们自己的任务，瓦莱莎。

column5: Right, of course.\nWant to lead the way?
column6: 对，当然。\n要带路吗？

column5: He nods, and then starts walking away from us.{w}\nWe gather together, and follow him close behind.
column6: 他点头，然后开始从我们身边走开。{w}\n我们聚到一起，紧跟在他身后。

column5: We're going to win this — I can feel it.
column6: 我们会赢的——我能感觉到。

column5: She smiles, and offers me her hand.{w}\nI grab it, and hold it as we follow Ulric.
column6: 她微笑着，向我伸出手。{w}\n我握住她的手，跟着乌尔里克前行。

column5: We're going to win this — I can feel it.
column6: 我们会赢的——我能感觉到。

column5: I pray, with every fiber of my being, that she's right.{w}\nAfter what seems like an eternity, The Triumvirate's castle comes into view.{w}\nI've never been more terrified in my life. The end was finally within reach.
column6: 我发自肺腑地祈祷她是对的。{w}\n仿佛过了永恒那么久，三人执政团的城堡出现在视野中。{w}\n我一生中从未如此恐惧。终局终于近在眼前。

column5: The castle looks just as corrupt and decaying as everything else.{w}\nAlmost even moreso — like it could be the source of all this death.{w}\nAs we get closer, I look all over the exterior. Then, I see Fortaime.
column6: 那座城堡看起来和其他一切一样腐败、破败。{w}\n甚至更甚——仿佛它正是这一切死亡的源头。{w}\n走近时，我打量着城堡的外墙。然后，我看见了福泰姆。

column5: He's climbing the tower, just as directed. It's a sight to behold.{w}\nIf he could get to that belltower, then the war would surely be ours.{w}\nBut I see him struggling. This castle was clearly his hardest climb.
column6: 他正按指示攀爬那座塔。那景象令人叹为观止。{w}\n只要他能到达那座钟楼，这场战争就必定是我们的。{w}\n但我看到他挣扎着。这座城堡显然是他最难爬的一座。

column5: With no safety nets, any slip up would be fatal.{w}\nI try not to think about it as we arrive at the bridge to the castle.{w}\nMuch to our dismay — the bridge is completely covered in suits of armor.
column6: 没有任何安全防护，任何失足都会致命。{w}\n我们抵达通往城堡的桥时，我尽量不去想这件事。{w}\n令我们沮丧的是——桥上密密麻麻全是盔甲。

column5: They turn to face us as soon as we approach.{w}\nA few seconds later, they start to march toward us.{w}\nThey're slow. Our presence took some time to register.
column6: 我们一靠近，它们就转过头来面向我们。{w}\n几秒后，它们开始朝我们行进。{w}\n它们很慢。它们花了一点时间才察觉到我们的存在。

column5: Normally, I'd be confident. These things are easy to slay.{w}\nBut this was a veritable horde. Hundreds, maybe even a thousand.{w}\nIt must've been another group en route to the burning Grand Library.
column6: 平时我会很自信。这些东西很容易斩杀。{w}\n但这可是一支名副其实的大军。数百，甚至上千。{w}\n这一定是另一队正赶往燃烧的大图书馆的。

column5: Stay behind me. We can use this bridge to our benefit.\nThey can't get around us, or sneak up from behind.\nIt's almost like a funnel. This should be easy.
column6: 待在我身后。我们可以利用这座桥。\n它们没法绕过我们，也没法从背后偷袭。\n这几乎就像一个漏斗。应该很容易。

column5: Me and Valessa give Ulric a firm nod. Sovy stands by his side.{w}\nA moment later, in perfect unison, they both charge into the crowd.{w}\nThe Honor Guard stood no chance. Not against two former Grand Inquisitors.
column6: 我和瓦莱莎坚定地向乌尔里克点头。索维站在他身旁。{w}\n片刻后，两人默契十足地冲进人群。{w}\n荣誉卫队毫无胜算。对手可是两位前大审判官。

column5: The suits start to crumble and fall as they fight across the bridge.{w}\nUlric's greatsword, and Sovy's fists kill almost ten or more each second.{w}\nHowever, as I look to the back — I notice a bunch of suits have bows.
column6: 他们一路杀过桥去，那些盔甲开始碎裂倒下。{w}\n乌尔里克的巨剑和索维的拳头每秒都能杀死将近十个甚至更多。{w}\n然而，当我望向后方——我注意到有一群盔甲拿着弓。

column5: I shout out to Ulric and Sovy, letting them know of the danger.
column6: 我朝乌尔里克和索维大喊，提醒他们危险。

column5: Me and Valessa give Ulric a firm nod.{w}\nA moment later, he charges into the crowd.{w}\nThey stood no chance. Ulric was too good at this.
column6: 我和瓦莱莎坚定地向乌尔里克点头。{w}\n片刻后，他冲进人群。{w}\n它们毫无胜算。乌尔里克太擅长这个了。

column5: The suits start to crumble and fall apart as he crosses the bridge.{w}\nWide swings of his greatsword take out almost ten at a time.{w}\nBut I notice a large portion of the horde at the back has bows.
column6: 他穿过桥时，那些盔甲开始碎裂、崩塌。{w}\n他巨剑一挥横扫，一次就能撂倒将近十个。{w}\n但我注意到后方很大一部分追兵拿着弓。

column5: I shout out to him, letting him know of the danger.
column6: 我朝他大喊，提醒他危险。

column5: I know — but don't worry, these things have bad aim.\nJust grab one of those suits and use them as a shield.\nThey'll wear out their numbers by killing their own.
column6: 我知道——但别担心，这些东西准头很差。\n抓一个那些盔甲当盾牌就行。\n它们会用自己的命来消耗自己的数量。

column5: I suppose that's a good strategy.{w}\nAfter I unsheathe The Blade of Exodus, I step forward.{w}\nMy goal is to find a good opening, so I can hop in and assist them.

column5: But no such opening comes. They slay with unmatched expertise.{w}\nThe two fight side by side, as if they're one entity. Perfect synergy.{w}\nMe and Valessa notice the archers at the back prepare to shoot.
column6: 但并没有这样的机会出现。他们以无与伦比的技艺斩杀着。{w}\n两人并肩作战，仿佛浑然一体。配合天衣无缝。{w}\n我和瓦莱莎注意到后方的弓箭手准备射击。

column5: But no such opening comes. He's slaying them with unseen expertise.{w}\nMe and Valessa notice the archers at the back prepare to shoot.

column5: Quick — grab one...!
column6: 快——抓一个……！

column5: We both rush forward, and each disarm one of the enemies.{w}\nWith no means to fight us back, we hold them in place.{w}\nAny arrows coming our way would hit them first.
column6: 我们两人一起冲上前，各自缴了一个敌人的械。{w}\n它们无法反击，被我们制在原地。{w}\n任何射向我们的箭都会先射中它们。

column5: A perfect plan — if that's actually what the archers were planning.{w}\nMuch to our shock, as the chaos on the bridge unfolds, they turn around.{w}\nThey're no longer aiming in our direction. They're aiming straight for Fortaime!
column6: 完美的计划——如果那真是弓箭手们的打算的话。{w}\n令我们震惊的是，当桥上的混乱展开时，它们转过身去。{w}\n它们不再瞄准我们这个方向。它们径直瞄准了福泰姆！

column5: Fortaime! Look out!
column6: 福泰姆！小心！

column5: Her calls fall upon deaf ears. He was too far away to hear.{w}\nThere was no way for any of us to prevent what happened next.{w}\nThey let their arrows fly. Some miss, but one pierces Fortaime's side.
column6: 她的呼喊落进了聋子的耳朵。他离得太远，听不见。{w}\n我们谁也无法阻止接下来发生的事。{w}\n它们放箭了。有些射偏了，但有一支射穿了福泰姆的侧身。

column5: He immediately starts to lose his grip, and it appears that he may fall off.{w}\nThere's nothing we could do. We can't call out to him, or get up there to help.{w}\nI have to do something quickly! They're preparing to shoot at him again...!
column6: 他立刻开始抓不稳，看来可能会摔下来。{w}\n我们无能为力。我们既喊不到他，也上不去帮他。{w}\n我得赶快做点什么！它们正准备再次朝他射箭……！

column5: Quick — run along the side of the bridge!\nIt should be wide enough to use as a path.\nGet back there, and take out those archers!
column6: 快——沿着桥的侧面跑过去！\n那里应该够宽，能当路走。\n绕到后面去，干掉那些弓箭手！

column5: I don't take her suggestion to heart. I have my own idea.{w}\nRunning forward, and pushing Ulric and Sovy out of the way, I ready my sword.{w}\nThey'd pay for hurting my friend. Every single one of them would pay...!
column6: 我没把她的建议放在心上。我有自己的主意。{w}\n我冲上前去，把乌尔里克和索维推开，举起我的剑。{w}\n它们伤害我的朋友，必须付出代价。它们每一个都得付出代价……！

column5: I don't take her suggestion to heart. I have my own idea.{w}\nRunning forward, and pushing Ulric out of the way, I ready my sword.{w}\nThey'd pay for hurting my friend. Every single one of them would pay...!

column5: I thrust the blade through one of the suits, then look over at Fortaime.{w}\nHe looks so weak, and delirious. Moments later, he falls from the tower.{w}\nThat sight alone is enough to fill me with more rage than I've ever felt before.
column6: 我把剑刺穿其中一具盔甲，然后望向福泰姆。{w}\n他看起来那么虚弱、神志不清。片刻后，他从塔上坠落。{w}\n仅这一幕，就足以让我心中充满前所未有的怒火。

column5: Activating the blade, that familiar flash of white light blinds all of us.{w}\nI can hear my allies struggling, as if they're still fighting while blinded.{w}\nBut a few seconds later, I hear nothing but the shattering of every suit of armor.
column6: 激活剑的力量，那道熟悉的白光刺得我们都睁不开眼。{w}\n我能听见同伴们在挣扎，仿佛他们仍在目不能视的情况下战斗。{w}\n但几秒后，我听到的只有每一具盔甲碎裂的声音。

column5: As the light subsides, we're greeted to the sight of victory.{w}\nEvery member of The Honor Guard on the bridge was dead.{w}\nI absorbed them into the blade — making it even stronger.
column6: 光芒消退，迎接我们的是胜利的景象。{w}\n桥上每一个荣誉卫队成员都死了。{w}\n我把它们吸入了剑中——让它变得更加强大。

column5: Huh...?
[firstname]...? Did you do that?
column6: [firstname]……？是你干的吗？

column5: I nod. I tell them I used the emotion inside of me as a catalyst.{w}\nThe emotion from seeing Fortaime fall, perhaps to his death.{w}\nAs we glance over to the tower though — I see that I was wrong.
column6: 我点头。我告诉他们，我把自己内心的情绪当作催化剂。{w}\n那是看到福泰姆坠落、也许就此丧命时产生的情绪。{w}\n然而当我们望向塔楼时——我发现我错了。

column5: He holds on to the edge of a window, and struggles to climb inside.{w}\nSo he {i}wanted{/i} to drop. To fall to a window, and get inside to safety.{w}\nI can see that his clothes are covered in blood from the arrow wound.
column6: 他抓住一扇窗户的边缘，挣扎着爬进去。{w}\n所以他{i}是故意{/i}跳下来的。跳到一扇窗边，然后爬进里面安全的地方。{w}\n我能看到，他衣服上沾满了箭伤流出的血。

column5: Eventually, he makes it inside, and we're all relieved.{w}\nFor a few seconds there, it seemed like all hope was lost.
column6: 最终，他成功进去了，我们都松了口气。{w}\n那几秒钟里，仿佛一切希望都破灭了。

column5: Thanks for stepping in like that.\nMy sword arm was starting to get a little tired.\nCome on, let's get going. We don't have much time.
column6: 谢谢你那样出手相助。\n我这条使剑的手臂都有点累了。\n来吧，我们走。时间不多了。

column5: Me, Sovy, and Ulric smile at one another.{w}\nValessa however, has a look of shock on her face.
column6: 我、索维和乌尔里克相视而笑。{w}\n然而瓦莱莎脸上却是一副震惊的神情。

column5: Ulric and I smile at one another.{w}\nValessa however, has a look of shock on her face.
column6: 我和乌尔里克相视而笑。{w}\n然而瓦莱莎脸上却是一副震惊的神情。

column5: Oh no...
column6: 哦不……

column5: We turn to face the same direction as her.{w}\nShe's looking back, toward the Town Square, and the bulk of the battle.{w}\nAnother horde is marching in our direction, likely attracted by the light.
column6: 我们朝她望的方向转过头去。{w}\n她正回望着城镇广场，以及战斗最激烈的地方。{w}\n又一大群追兵正朝我们行进，多半是被那道光吸引来的。

column5: Just our luck.
column6: 真是我们的运气。

column5: We all ready our weapons.
column6: 我们都准备好了武器。

column5: Ulric readies his sword.
column6: 乌尔里克准备好了他的剑。

column5: We watch them walk toward us in unison.{w}\nAn unease fills the air. I doubt I could deactivate {i}all{/i} of them.{w}\nI only did that thanks to the surge of emotion from seeing Fortaime shot.
column6: 我们看着它们步伐一致地朝我们走来。{w}\n空气中弥漫着不安。我怀疑自己无法让{i}所有{/i}它们都停下。{w}\n我之所以能做到，只是靠看到福泰姆中箭时那股情绪爆发而已。

column5: It wouldn't be right for me to rely on something like that yet again.{w}\nPart of me wonders if we should flee inside and fight them off in the castle.{w}\nBut we had no idea what awaited us inside, or if Pro was even successful.
column6: 我不该再一次依赖那样的东西。{w}\n我有一部分在想，我们是否该躲进去，在城堡里击退它们。{w}\n但我们不知道里面等着我们的是什么，也不知道普洛是否成功了。

column5: Valessa steps forward, standing in front of us.{w}\nShe trembles, perhaps terrified of what's to come.
column6: 瓦莱莎上前一步，站在我们面前。{w}\n她颤抖着，也许是害怕即将到来的一切。

column5: You need to go.
column6: 你们得走。

column5: What are you talking about...?
column6: 你在说什么……？

column5: I said you need to go. Get inside the castle!\nHelp Fortaime, kill The Triumvirate — just do it!\nLet me keep them occupied. I'll fight them off.
column6: 我说了你们得走。进城堡里去！\n去帮福泰姆，去杀三人执政团——快去做！\n让我拖住它们。我来击退它们。

column5: Valessa, that's suicide.
column6: 瓦莱莎，那是自杀。

column5: We don't have any other option.\n[firstname] {i}needs{/i} you and Ulric.
column6: 我们别无选择。\n[firstname]{i}需要{/i}你和乌尔里克。

column5: No — {i}I'll{/i} stay and fight.\nI know how those things work.
column6: 不——{i}我{/i}留下来打。\n我知道那些东西是怎么回事。

column5: This isn't up for debate.\nYou need to go. Now.
column6: 这没得商量。\n你们得走。马上。

column5: Sovy backs down, realizing there's no point.{w}\nEach second needed to be filled with action, not inaction.{w}\nIf we wasted time, we'd just hand victory over to the enemy.
column6: 索维退让了，意识到争论没有意义。{w}\n每一秒都必须用行动来填充，而不是空耗。{w}\n如果我们浪费时间，就等于把胜利拱手让给敌人。

column5: What are you talking about...?

column5: I can't let you throw your life away, Valessa.
column6: 我不能让你白白送命，瓦莱莎。

column5: This isn't up for debate. Sorry.\nYou need to go — and fast.
column6: 这没得商量。抱歉。\n你们得走——而且要快。

column5: Ulric backs down, realizing there's no point.{w}\nEach second needed to be filled with action, not inaction.{w}\nIf we wasted time, we'd just hand victory over to the enemy.
column6: 乌尔里克退让了，意识到争论没有意义。{w}\n每一秒都必须用行动来填充，而不是空耗。{w}\n如果我们浪费时间，就等于把胜利拱手让给敌人。

column5: Valessa pulls out her Mother's daggers with a gulp.{w}\nI guess taking them from Mazeo was a good idea after all.{w}\nMy mind tells me to talk her out of this, but I say nothing.
column6: 瓦莱莎咽了口唾沫，拔出她母亲的匕首。{w}\n看来从马泽奥把它们带出来，终究是个好主意。{w}\n我理智上想劝她别这样，却什么也没说。

column5: Valessa crouches down and picks up an enemy's sword.{w}\nShe swings it a few times, testing its weight, and then nods.{w}\nMy mind tells me to talk her out of this, but I say nothing.
column6: 瓦莱莎蹲下，捡起一把敌人的剑。{w}\n她挥舞了几下，试试分量，然后点点头。{w}\n我理智上想劝她别这样，却什么也没说。

column5: If she fought hard enough, she'd be able to survive.{w}\nThose suits are weak, and mindless. I feel like she'd be okay.{w}\nI justify her choice in my mind, perhaps because I know it's inevitable.
column6: 只要她拼得够狠，就能活下来。{w}\n那些盔甲既弱又没脑子。我觉得她会没事的。{w}\n我在心里为她的选择找理由，也许是因为我知道这已无法避免。

column5: She wraps her arms around me and gives me a tight hug.{w}\nI return it, and then she looks up at me, and kisses my lips.{w}\nAfter teling her that I love her, I tell her to stay safe, and survive.
column6: 她张开双臂，紧紧抱住我。{w}\n我也回抱她，然后她抬头看着我，吻上我的唇。{w}\n我告诉她我爱她，然后让她注意安全，活下去。

column5: Is that an order...?
column6: 这是命令吗……？

column5: Yeah.
column6: 是啊。

column5: Then I guess I have no choice.\nI love you, [firstname]. Never forget that.\nI'll see you in the atrium when this is all over.
column6: 那我大概别无选择了。\n我爱你，[firstname]。永远别忘了。\n等这一切结束后，我们在中庭见。

column5: She wraps her arms around me, and gives me a tight hug.{w}\nI know that this may be the last time we see each other, and it hurts.{w}\nWe've come so far since our time in Valinorth; and changed so much.
column6: 她张开双臂，紧紧抱住我。{w}\n我知道这也许是我们最后一次相见，这让我心痛。{w}\n自瓦利诺斯那段时光以来，我们走了这么远，也改变了这么多。

column5: Thanks for everything you've done, [firstname].
column6: 谢谢你做的一切，[firstname]。

column5: I tell her to stay safe, and survive.{w}\nA moment later, the tight hug is broken.
column6: 我让她注意安全，活下去。{w}\n片刻后，那个紧紧的拥抱松开了。

column5: Oh? Is that an order?
column6: 哦？这是命令吗？

column5: Yeah.
column6: 是啊。

column5: Then I guess I have no choice.\nI've never disobeyed, and I'm not about to start.\nI'll meet you in the atrium after Fortaime rings that bell.
column6: 那我大概别无选择了。\n我从未违抗过，也不打算现在开始。\n等福泰姆敲响那口钟后，我们在中庭见。

column5: And a moment later, we're both off in opposite directions.{w}\nBut as we head toward the castle, I can't help but look back.{w}\nI'm both worried, and hopeful, and both sides are at war.
column6: 片刻后，我们各自朝着相反的方向离去。{w}\n但当我们朝城堡走去时，我忍不住回头望。{w}\n我既担忧又满怀希望，两种心情在心里交战。

column5: I see her charge into the crowd, holding out her daggers.{w}\nThe sound of her stabbing the suits soon fills the air.{w}\nThey fall apart, and hit the ground with loud thuds.
column6: 我看见她举着匕首冲进人群。{w}\n她刺击那些盔甲的声音很快充斥空气。{w}\n它们崩解开来，重重地砸在地上。

column5: Come on — I could do this all day...!
column6: 来吧——我能这样打一整天……！

column5: With a smirk on my face, I realize her victory is clear.{w}\nWe retreat into the castle, and the sight makes my jaw drop.{w}\nThe castle is hauntingly beautiful. Like nothing I've seen before.
column6: 我嘴角一扬，明白她的胜利已成定局。{w}\n我们退入城堡，眼前的景象让我目瞪口呆。{w}\n这座城堡美得摄人心魄。是我从未见过的样子。

column5: As we venture forward, I can only hope that Pro was successful.{w}\nThe bell hasn't rung yet, but I have the utmost faith in Fortaime's ability.{w}\nI let out a deep sigh of relief. I'm here, in their castle. This is the end.
column6: 我们向前深入时，我只能希望普洛成功了。{w}\n钟还没响，但我对福泰姆的能力有十足的信心。{w}\n我如释重负地长舒一口气。我到了，就在他们的城堡里。这就是终局。

column5: I see her charge into the crowd, holding out the sword.{w}\nShe starts swinging it, taking out a ton of suits with her strength.{w}\nThey fall apart, and hit the ground with loud thuds. She was doing this...!
column6: 我看见她举着剑冲进人群。{w}\n她开始挥舞，凭着蛮力撂倒一大片盔甲。{w}\n它们崩解开来，重重地砸在地上。她真的做到了……！

column5: Come on — I could do this all day...!
column6: 来吧——我能这样打一整天……！

column5: With a smirk on my face, I realize that her victory is clear.{w}\nHowever — a moment later — I'm shocked at my arrogance.{w}\nMuch like before, the rear of the horde readies some bows.
column6: 我嘴角一扬，明白她的胜利已成定局。{w}\n然而——片刻之后——我为自己的傲慢感到震惊。{w}\n和之前一样，那群追兵的后方架起了几把弓。

column5: I had to warn her...!{w}\nI shout out, and start to run toward her.{w}\nHowever, Ulric grabs my arm, stopping me.
column6: 我必须提醒她……！{w}\n我大喊着，开始朝她跑去。{w}\n然而乌尔里克抓住我的手臂，拦住了我。

column5: We need to get inside, [firstname].\nThere's no time to waste. You have to trust her.\nShe volunteered for this. She knows what she's doing.
column6: 我们得进去，[firstname]。\n没时间可浪费了。你得相信她。\n这是她自愿的。她清楚自己在做什么。

column5: I struggle some more, but his grip is far too strong.{w}\nI yield, and follow Ulric into the castle, still looking back.{w}\nThe next thing I see, will forever be etched into my mind.
column6: 我又挣扎了几下，但他的力气太大。{w}\n我屈服了，跟着乌尔里克进了城堡，仍不停地回头望。{w}\n接下来我看到的景象，将永远刻在我脑海里。

column5: The archers let their arrows loose, and several hit Valessa.{w}\nShe screams, and stumbles back, blood marring her outfit.{w}\nBut she doesn't give up. She keeps fighting, with all of her might.
column6: 弓箭手放出了箭，好几支射中了瓦莱莎。{w}\n她尖叫着，踉跄后退，鲜血玷污了她的衣裳。{w}\n但她没有放弃。她拼尽全力，继续战斗。

column5: They let their arrows loose again, and she's pierced even further.{w}\nNobody would survive such blows, but she fights on with determination.{w}\nA pool of blood gathers beneath her; and that's the last thing I see.
column6: 它们再次放箭，她被射得更深。{w}\n没人能挨得住这样的伤，她却仍带着决心战斗下去。{w}\n她身下积起一滩血；那是我看到的最后景象。

column5: She may continue fighting, and buying time, but those wounds were fatal.{w}\nWe retreat fully into the castle, and the gruesome scene is soon out of view.{w}\nAnger wells up within me. Whoever opposed me next? I surely pitied them.
column6: 她或许还在继续战斗、争取时间，但那些伤是致命的。{w}\n我们完全退入城堡，那惨烈的一幕很快离开了视野。{w}\n怒火在我心中涌起。下一个挡在我面前的人？我肯定会为他感到可怜。

column5: Eventually, Pro and Gryz's path lead them to a large hallway.{w}\nPlenty of open space to fight, and destroy the horde in pursuit of them.{w}\nThe distraction worked perfectly. Now they just had to deal with the company.
column6: 最终，普洛和格瑞兹的路把他们引到一条宽阔的走廊。{w}\n有足够的开阔空间战斗，消灭追赶他们的那群追兵。{w}\n诱敌之计完美奏效。现在他们只需应付这些“客人”了。

column5: Pro — what weapons do you have...?
column6: 普洛——你有什么武器……？

column5: Gryz readies his large warhammer.
column6: 格瑞兹举起他那把巨大的战锤。

column5: Daggers — my favorite.\nUp close and personal.
column6: 匕首——我的最爱。\n近距离，面对面。

column5: He draws them, and stands beside Gryz.
column6: 他抽出匕首，站到格瑞兹身旁。

column5: So, you've fought these things before?
column6: 那么，你以前和这些东西打过？

column5: Yeah — plenty of times.\nIt'll be a piece of cake. Trust me.
column6: 是啊——打过很多次。\n小事一桩。相信我。

column5: Right.
column6: 好吧。

column5: A few moments pass, and The Honor Guard finally catches up with them.{w}\nThe horde seems to have tripled in size. Everything was going their way.{w}\nAt this rate, The Monarch should have almost no opposition at all.
column6: 过了片刻，荣誉卫队终于追上了他们。{w}\n那群追兵似乎扩大了三倍。一切都在按他们的计划发展。{w}\n照这势头，君主那边应该几乎不会遇到什么抵抗。

column5: Be mindful of where you stand, Pro.\nIf this hammer is good at anything, it's crowd control.\nI don't want to hit you while I'm fighting off the enemy.
column6: 注意你站的位置，普洛。\n要说这锤子擅长什么，那就是控制人群。\n我不想在对付敌人时误伤到你。

column5: Yeah — got it.\nI'll stay low, and out of your way.
column6: 是啊——明白。\n我会压低身子，不挡你的路。

column5: Gryz nods, and they stand side by side as enemies fill the room.
column6: 格瑞兹点头，敌人涌满房间时，两人并肩而立。

column5: Ready...?
column6: 准备好了吗……？

column5: Pro gulps.
column6: 普洛咽了口唾沫。

column5: Let's do this.
column6: 动手吧。

column5: They charge into the crowd, and the fight begins.{w}\nPro makes sure to stay below shoulder height as Gryz swings his hammer.{w}\nHe takes out about ten or more suits with every swing of that mighty weapon.
column6: 他们冲进人群，战斗开始了。{w}\n格瑞兹挥锤时，普洛刻意保持在肩膀以下的高度。{w}\n那件威力惊人的武器每一挥，都能撂倒十个甚至更多的盔甲。

column5: Pro rolls on the floor, taking them out with precise stabs to the abdomen.{w}\nShattering like glass, the suits are falling at a rate that guarantees their victory.{w}\nBoth men pant from exertion as they fight what was hopefully their last fight.
column6: 普洛在地上翻滚，精准地刺向它们的腹部，将其一一解决。{w}\n盔甲像玻璃般碎裂，倒下的速度快得足以保证他们的胜利。{w}\n两人气喘吁吁，奋力搏杀——但愿这是他们最后一场战斗。
